# link-destination-style

- ID: `MDL001`
- Category: Links and images
- Default: on, severity warning
- Fixable: no
- Tags: `links`, `url`

Relative links and local file: URLs are not mixed in one document.

## Why

Relative and absolute links behave differently when a file moves or a repository
is forked. One kind keeps that behavior the same for every link that could take
either form. A link to another host, such as https\://example.com, cannot be
relative, so it never counts. gomdlint cannot tell a URL of the document's own
site from one of another host, so the only absolute links that count are file:
URLs that name no other host. URIs such as mailto:, autolinks and links to a
\#fragment never count either.

## Options

Set them under `rules.link-destination-style.options`.

- `style` (`string`, default `consistent`): Kind of link destination to require:
  relative paths or absolute URLs. Only relative links and file: URLs that name
  no other host count. consistent takes the kind of the first link that counts.
  Values: `consistent`, `relative`, `absolute`.

## Fix

There is no automatic fix.

## Example

This document breaks the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

- [Install](docs/install.md)
- [Configure](file:///home/ana/gomdlint/docs/configure.md)
```

gomdlint reports:

```text
4:3 Link uses absolute URL, but relative URLs are expected
```

This document follows the rule:

```markdown
# Guide

- [Install](docs/install.md)
- [Configure](docs/configure.md)
```

## Configure

```yaml
rules:
  link-destination-style:
    options:
      style: consistent
```

Under `rules`, `link-destination-style: false` turns the rule off and
`link-destination-style: error` reports its findings as errors. The flag
`--disable link-destination-style` turns it off for one run.

## Silence one line

```markdown
<!-- markdownlint-disable-next-line link-destination-style -->
```

## markdownlint

markdownlint does not have this rule.
